title: Tech Bros to Cowboys: How Much Better Off Are Californians Who Move to Texas?
description:
Compares recent California-to-Texas movers against Californians who stayed, using American Community Survey microdata (2021–2023, n = 981,006) and BEA regional price parities. Holding demographics, education, and household composition fixed, movers have income relative to a locally-priced poverty threshold 10.1% higher (95% CI 3.7% to 16.9%, p = 0.002). Against the unadjusted federal threshold the same comparison shows no detectable difference (−3.9%, p = 0.19): the gain consists entirely of purchasing power, which the official measure is designed not to see. These are descriptive comparisons, not causal effects.

This deposit contains the paper (reports/paper.pdf) and the full Python pipeline. Paper text and figures are CC BY 4.0; source code is MIT (see LICENSE). IPUMS microdata is not redistributed.
